### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [...], rhs_batching_dimensions = [...], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [...], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [...]>} : (T_a, T_b) -> T_r`; empty batching fields optional. lhs and rhs must have the same element type. The result dimensions are, in order, the batch dimensions, then the remaining lhs dimensions in their original order, then the remaining rhs dimensions in their original order. Each paired batch dimension and each paired contracting dimension must have equal sizes on the lhs and the rhs. The lhs and rhs must list the same number of batch dimensions and the same number of contracting dimensions, and no dimension may be both a batch and a contracting dimension. Each result element is the sum, over all contracting indices, of products of lhs and rhs elements at the same batch index; there is no implicit transpose, so the choice of contracting dimensions decides which axes are summed.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires.

transpose is written `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: 1, 0>} : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. Result dimension d has the size of operand dimension permutation[d]. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. 
### stablehlo.convert
convert is written `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (T_in) -> T_out`.

The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.convolution
convolution is written `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%x, %w) {window_strides = array<i64: 1, 1>, padding = dense<[[1, 1], [1, 1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]>, feature_group_count = 1 : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (tensor<2x3x8x8xf32>, tensor<4x3x3x3xf32>) -> tensor<2x4x8x8xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. Each output spatial size is floor((low + (n - 1) * lhs_dilation + 1 + high - ((k - 1) * rhs_dilation + 1)) / stride) + 1, where n is the input size and k the kernel size along that dimension. The kernel's input-feature size equals the input feature size divided by feature_group_count, and the kernel's output-feature size, which becomes the output feature size, must be divisible by feature_group_count. convolution computes a cross-correlation without flipping the kernel; rhs_dilation spaces out kernel taps (dilated convolution), lhs_dilation inserts lhs_dilation - 1 zeros between input elements (used for transposed convolution together with a spatially reversed kernel), and feature_group_count splits the features into independent groups (grouped or depthwise convolution).

Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [...], rhs_batching_dimensions = [...], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [...], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [...]>} : (T_a, T_b) -> T_r`; empty batching fields optional. lhs and rhs must have the same element type. The result dimensions are, in order, the batch dimensions, then the remaining lhs dimensions in their original order, then the remaining rhs dimensions in their original order. Each paired batch dimension and each paired contracting dimension must have equal sizes on the lhs and the rhs. The lhs and rhs must list the same number of batch dimensions and the same number of contracting dimensions, and no dimension may be both a batch and a contracting dimension. Each result element is the sum, over all contracting indices, of products of lhs and rhs elements at the same batch index; there is no implicit transpose, so the choice of contracting dimensions decides which axes are summed.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.convolution
convolution is written `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%x, %w) {window_strides = array<i64: 1, 1>, padding = dense<[[1, 1], [1, 1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]>, feature_group_count = 1 : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (tensor<2x3x8x8xf32>, tensor<4x3x3x3xf32>) -> tensor<2x4x8x8xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. Each output spatial size is floor((low + (n - 1) * lhs_dilation + 1 + high - ((k - 1) * rhs_dilation + 1)) / stride) + 1, where n is the input size and k the kernel size along that dimension. The kernel's input-feature size equals the input feature size divided by feature_group_count, and the kernel's output-feature size, which becomes the output feature size, must be divisible by feature_group_count. convolution computes a cross-correlation without flipping the kernel; rhs_dilation spaces out kernel taps (dilated convolution), lhs_dilation inserts lhs_dilation - 1 zeros between input elements (used for transposed convolution together with a spatially reversed kernel), and feature_group_count splits the features into independent groups (grouped or depthwise convolution). 
### stablehlo.reverse
reverse is written `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3x2xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T) -> T`. The result has the operand's type, and dimensions are distinct indices between 0 and the rank minus one. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a series of operations: Gemm, Subtract, GlobalAvgPool, LogSumExp, GELU, and ResidualAdd.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, bias=True):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.gemm = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features, bias=bias)
        self.subtract = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features))

    def forward(self, x):
        original_x = x.clone().detach()
        # Gemm
        x = self.gemm(x)

        # Subtract
        x = x - self.subtract

        # GlobalAvgPool
        x = torch.mean(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # LogSumExp
        x = torch.logsumexp(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # GELU
        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)

        # ResidualAdd
        x = x + original_x

        return x

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a series of operations: Gemm, Subtract, GlobalAvgPool, LogSumExp, GELU, and ResidualAdd.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, bias=True):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.gemm = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features, bias=bias)
        self.subtract = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features))

    def forward(self, x):
        original_x = x.clone().detach()
        # Gemm
        x = self.gemm(x)

        # Subtract
        x = x - self.subtract

        # GlobalAvgPool
        x = torch.mean(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # LogSumExp
        x = torch.logsumexp(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # GELU
        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)

        # ResidualAdd
        x = x + original_x

        return x

in_features = 7
out_features = 7

def get_inputs():
    return [torch.rand(batch_size, in_features)]

def get_init_inputs():
    return [in_features, out_features]

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dot_general

The lhs and rhs must list the same number of batch dimensions and the same number of contracting dimensions, and no dimension may be both a batch and a contracting dimension. import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a series of operations: Gemm, Subtract, GlobalAvgPool, LogSumExp, GELU, and ResidualAdd.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, bias=True):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.gemm = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features, bias=bias)
        self.subtract = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_features))

    def forward(self, x):
        original_x = x.clone().detach()
        # Gemm
        x = self.gemm(x)

        # Subtract
        x = x - self.subtract

        # GlobalAvgPool
        x = torch.mean(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # LogSumExp
        x = torch.logsumexp(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)

        # GELU
        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)

        # ResidualAdd
        x = x + original_x

        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs a matrix multiplication, adds a value, applies Swish, Tanh, GELU, and Hardtanh activation functions.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, add_value_shape):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.matmul = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)
        self.add_value = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(add_value_shape)) 

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.matmul(x)
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.sigmoid(x) * x # Swish
        x = torch.tanh(x)
        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x) # GELU

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs a matrix multiplication, adds a value, applies Swish, Tanh, GELU, and Hardtanh activation functions.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, add_value_shape):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.matmul = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)
        self.add_value = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(add_value_shape)) 

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.matmul(x)
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.sigmoid(x) * x # Swish

        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x) # GELU
        x = torch.nn.functional.hardtanh(x, min_val=-1, max_val=1) # Hardtanh
        return x

One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs).         out_channels (int): Number of channels produced by the convolution.

        return self.conv_transpose2d(x)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Performs a depthwise-separable 2D convolution operation.

    Args:
        in_channels (int): Number of channels in the input tensor.
        out_channels (int): Number of channels produced by the convolution.
        kernel_size (int): Size of the convolution kernel.
        stride (int, optional): Stride of the convolution. Defaults to 1.
        padding (int, optional): Padding applied to the input. Defaults to 0.
        dilation (int, optional): Spacing between kernel elements. Defaults to 1.
        bias (bool, optional): If `True`, adds a learnable bias to the output. Defaults to `False`.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int, kernel_size: int, stride: int = 1, padding: int = 0, dilation: int = 1, bias: bool = False):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.depthwise = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding, dilation=dilation, groups=in_channels, bias=bias)
        self.pointwise = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=bias)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Performs the depthwise-separable 2D convolution.

        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of shape (batch_size, in_channels, height, width).

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, height_out, width_out).
        """
        x = self.depthwise(x)
        x = self.pointwise(x)
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.slice
slice is written `%r = "stablehlo.slice"(%x) {start_indices = array<i64: 1, 0>, limit_indices = array<i64: 3, 4>, strides = array<i64: 1, 2>} : (tensor<4x4xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.slice"(%x) {start_indices = array<i64: ...>, limit_indices = array<i64: ...>, strides = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. start_indices, limit_indices and strides each have one entry per operand dimension. Starts and limits satisfy 0 <= start <= limit <= dimension size, limits are exclusive, and strides are positive. Each result dimension has size ceil((limit - start) / stride). class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Performs a depthwise-separable 2D convolution operation.

    Args:
        in_channels (int): Number of channels in the input tensor.
        out_channels (int): Number of channels produced by the convolution.
        kernel_size (int): Size of the convolution kernel.
        stride (int, optional): Stride of the convolution. Defaults to 1.
        padding (int, optional): Padding applied to the input. Defaults to 0.
        dilation (int, optional): Spacing between kernel elements. Defaults to 1.
        bias (bool, optional): If `True`, adds a learnable bias to the output. Defaults to `False`.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int, kernel_size: int, stride: int = 1, padding: int = 0, dilation: int = 1, bias: bool = False):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.depthwise = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, in_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding, dilation=dilation, groups=in_channels, bias=bias)

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, height_out, width_out).
        """
        x = self.depthwise(x)
        x = self.pointwise(x)
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose.

The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.convert
convert is written `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same shape as the operand; only the element type changes. Float-to-integer conversion truncates the fractional part toward zero, a boolean converts to 0 or 1, and a number converts to a boolean as true exactly when it is non-zero. 
### stablehlo.dynamic_slice
dynamic_slice takes the operand followed by one rank-0 integer start index per dimension: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %i, %j) {slice_sizes = array<i64: 2, 4>} : (tensor<8x4xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<2x4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %s0, ..., %s_{R-1}) {slice_sizes = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<I>, ...) -> T_out`. All start indices are rank-0 tensors of the same integer type, and the result element type equals the operand's. class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a convolution, adds a bias term, scales, applies sigmoid, and performs group normalization.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, num_groups, bias_shape, scale_shape):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)

        x = torch.sigmoid(x)
        x = self.group_norm(x)
        return x

    """
    Model that performs a matrix multiplication (Gemm), followed by LogSumExp, LeakyReLU, 
    LeakyReLU, GELU, and GELU activations.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, bias=True):

One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, applies Mish activation, adds a value, 
    applies Hardtanh activation, and scales the output.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, add_value, scale):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding)
        self.add_value = add_value
        self.scale = scale

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.nn.functional.mish(x) # Mish activation
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.nn.functional.hardtanh(x, min_val=-1, max_val=1) # Hardtanh activation
        x = x * self.scale # Scaling
        return x

In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`.

    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, add_value, scale):

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, applies Mish activation, adds a value, 
    applies Hardtanh activation, and scales the output.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, add_value, scale):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding)
        self.add_value = add_value
        self.scale = scale

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.nn.functional.mish(x) # Mish activation
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.nn.functional.hardtanh(x, min_val=-1, max_val=1) # Hardtanh activation
        x = x * self.scale # Scaling
        return x

The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

"stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`.     def __init__(self, input_size, hidden_size, num_groups, eps=1e-5, negative_slope=0.01):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.fc = nn.Linear(input_size, hidden_size)

        x = self.gn(x)
        x = self.leaky_relu(x)
        x = x + x
        return x

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a 3D convolution, scales the output, applies tanh, multiplies by a scaling factor, and applies sigmoid.

    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, scaling_factor, bias_shape):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)

In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`.
